extracted.intended_audience: early-career postdoctoral researchers (life-sciences and cross-disciplinary) and their proposed host supervisors/referees applying for HFSP Long-Term (LTF) or Cross-Disciplinary (CDF) Fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting and assessing Human Frontier Science Program Long-Term and Cross-Disciplinary postdoctoral fellowship applications (award year 2019), including eligibility, allowable research scope, review criteria, award conditions, and administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scientific objective / alignment with HFSP scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program aims to promote basic research focused on elucidation of sophisticated and complex mechanisms of living organisms via international cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be basic research on biological mechanisms (molecular, cellular to systems level including cognitive functions). Applications should align with HFSP’s objective of international, frontier basic research; applications outside this scope may be screened out at eligibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of frontier, transformative and interdisciplinary research
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP strongly supports frontier, potentially transformative (‘out-of-the-box’) proposals and encourages applications for high-risk projects. The projects should be interdisciplinary in nature and should challenge existing paradigms using novel approaches and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals representing standard or incremental approaches, obvious next steps, or routine projects are less likely to receive funding. Applicants are expected to be exposed during the fellowship to new theories and methods that complement or build on their expertise. CDF applicants should describe biological techniques they will learn and how their skills will contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research not supported (exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP does not support routine projects, applied clinical/pharmaceutical (translational) research that does not address a fundamental biological problem, clinical/pharmaceutical development of treatments/drug candidates, environmental research directly concerned with agricultural issues or pollution/bioremediation monitoring, ecological projects to discover species or monitor habitats, and observational studies unless they address a specific biological question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: high-throughput screens without addressing fundamental biological problems; applied engineering/biotech/nanotech not addressing fundamental biology. Observational studies must address a specific (typically cellular or molecular) biological question to be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and host country eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate who is not a national from one of the supporting countries may apply only to work in an institution in one of the supporting countries; a national of a supporting country can apply to work in a research institution in any country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of supporting countries provided. For extraterritorial institutions (e.g., EMBL, ICGEB) the country where the lab is located is considered the host country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral degree (PhD) requirement and conferral timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A research doctorate (PhD) or equivalent doctoral-level degree with equivalent basic research experience must be conferred by the start of the fellowship (not required at submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PhD awarded, conferral date determines eligibility: degree must have been conferred in the 3 years prior to submission deadline (between 1 Sept. 2015 and 23 Aug. 2018). Exceptions only for eligible post-PhD career interruptions (illness, parental leave, full-time care for immediate family, military/civil service); unemployment or work outside science are not eligible interruption periods. Eligible interruption periods are not counted but remaining duration must be less than 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD not yet awarded — timing constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: If PhD not yet awarded at submission, the PhD must be conferred by 31 December 2019 at the latest and the fellowship cannot start before the PhD is officially conferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: lead-author full-length research paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have at least one lead author, full-length research paper (accepted, in press, published or on a pre-print server such as bioRxiv) in an international peer-reviewed journal or pre-print server by the submission deadline. The applicant must be single, first, or joint first author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint first authorship must be clearly stated. If standard practice makes first authorship impossible (e.g., alphabetical listing), explain in 'Additional Comments'. All papers must be in English; review articles or patents are not accepted. Electronic copies of lead author publications must be uploaded while preparing the application (cannot be uploaded after applicant submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: prior start at proposed host before cut-off date
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who started to work in the proposed host institution or host country prior to 1 April 2018 are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: excessive prior time in host country
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who on 1 April 2019 have spent more than 12 months (consecutive or not) in the proposed host country are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All research-related stays are counted (research positions, collaborations, internships, Master/PhD work, visiting scientist time, technician time, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: excessive prior time with proposed host supervisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who on 1 April 2019 have spent more than 12 months (consecutive or not) with their proposed host supervisor are not eligible, even if the supervisor relocated to another country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: returning to same institution for same/similar project
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot propose to return to an institution where they have worked in the past if they plan to pursue the same or a similar project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: proposing to work with prior collaborators or supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot propose to work with former scientific collaborators, former research supervisors, or any other scientist with whom the applicant has worked or published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: taking up fellowship in PhD country
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot propose to take up the HFSP fellowship in the country where they obtained their PhD, even if the applicant is not a national of that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates with dual nationalities may apply to work in one of their countries of nationality provided they have never lived or studied in that country or left during early childhood; such cases require contacting the Fellowship Office to claim an exemption and get approval prior to applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: intra-country laboratory move
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to move from one laboratory to another in the same country are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: for-profit research environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work in a for-profit research environment are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limits per person / prior awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant cannot submit more than one HFSP fellowship application in a competition year, and former Long-Term or Cross-Disciplinary Fellowship awardees cannot apply for a second HFSP fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host supervisor endorsement limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Host supervisors can endorse only one application (LTF or CDF) per competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed host supervisor may concurrently mentor HFSP fellows from previous award years and/or be part of an HFSP Research Grant team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to request exemptions prior to submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must contact the Fellowship Office prior to submitting their application if they want to claim an exemption to any stated requirements or criteria for ineligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any exemption must be approved by the Fellowship Office prior to applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: registration, submission and supporting sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register and submit via the HFSPO extranet; host supervisors and referees must register and submit their sections by the submission deadline. Applicants can only submit once host supervisors and referees have submitted their sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the online application form is required at submission (no further documents or signatures at this stage). Deadline for registration/initiation and submission provided. Applicants may update publication list via HFSPO website until 30 November 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process stages
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three steps: eligibility assessment (formal), expert review (two review committee members), and evaluation by the entire review committee (discussion at 3-day meeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications failing key requirements or misaligned with HFSP scope will not be sent for expert review. The process is confidential and feedback is not provided to unsuccessful applicants due to volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert review criterion: Excellence of the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Accomplishments and potential of the candidate relative to previous/current opportunities, and scientific leadership potential based on motivation, goals and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign ratings. Indicators for 'Outstanding' include exceptional productivity and impact from PhD work, extremely supportive referee letters, articulate and mature career goals; 'Excellent' and lower categories described in the guidelines (see indicators table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert review criterion: Excellence of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Training potential of the fellowship based on scientific originality and innovation; intellectual contribution of the applicant; clear departure from previous research is viewed favourably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: 'Outstanding'—highly innovative, ground-breaking approach, challenges existing paradigms, addresses important new problem/barrier, proposed and written by the applicant, significant departure from previous research. Lower categories include host-lab projects, moderate change, routine/incremental approaches, or poorly articulated projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert review criterion: Excellence of the host lab and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the host and host environment including access to infrastructure and collaborators; track record of the host supervisor based on career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: 'Outstanding'—stellar established lab or promising new lab, excellent infrastructure and collaborators, strongly enthusiastic host letter and likely strong mentorship. Lower categories describe insufficient infrastructure, generic/unenthusiastic host letters, or not internationally competitive labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No imposed weighting among selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO does not impose a weighting among the individual selection criteria; reviewers determine the overall rating based on the provided indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and non-renewability
rubrics_metrics.description: The HFSP postdoctoral fellowship can be held for up to 3 years, with no possibility for renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows may interrupt HFSPO support after the second year for up to two years while continuing postdoc work funded through other sources. The third year may be used to continue in host lab, return home, or move to another HFSP member country. Fellows are eligible to apply for HFSP Career Development Award at the end of fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive dedication and concurrent employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows cannot concurrently hold a LTF or CDF and another paid fellowship or employment position (salary support) from another organization; fellows must devote themselves entirely to their research project and may not engage in any other paid activity without HFSPO agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution can supplement awardee’s salary and/or research/travel costs. Unauthorized paid activity or concurrent salaried employment is not allowed without agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship start window and activation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must begin their fellowship between 1 April 2019 and 1 January 2020; at the start the fellow must have been working for less than 12 full months in the host institution/host country and the PhD must have been conferred when the fellowship is activated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on changing host supervisor, project, or transferring fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally it is not possible to change the host supervisor, the research project, or to transfer the fellowship to another institution (except in the third year). Any unauthorized change will lead to immediate termination of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only under exceptional circumstances may changes be made after the award is offered, pending re-evaluation by HFSPO Secretariat and/or Review Committee. Fellows planning changes must contact the Fellowship Office before deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award management: preferred financial administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred administrative approach is via an institutional account managed by the host institution payroll office; private bank management allowed only if institutional management is problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: No coverage of health insurance or institutional overheads
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO fellowships do not provide additional funds beyond stated allowances and do not cover health insurance or other benefits; institutional overheads, bench fees or indirect costs cannot be deducted from fellowship allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host may designate living allowance as gross salary and establish institutional employment contract allowing deductions for social security or health insurance; host may supplement fellowship to match institutional salary levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellow tax/responsibility disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellow responsible for determining tax liability in host/home countries; Fellowship Office cannot answer tax liability questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSPO cannot stay abreast of taxation laws in all countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living allowance — country-based living stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: Living allowance is a subsistence allowance based on the country in which the fellowship is carried out; if fellow repatriates or transfers in final year, new country rate applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of living allowances by country and year provided; HFSPO reserves right to review stipend levels; contact Fellowship Office for amounts in other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP fellows with children are entitled to receive an annual child allowance per child corresponding to about 10% of the first year living allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fellow receives child allowance from another source, that amount will be deducted from HFSP child allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental leave allowance and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may apply for up to 3 months of paid parental leave during the fellowship; parental leave must be initiated within 6 months of birth of the child (applies only to children born during the fellowship). The fellowship will be extended for the same duration as the parental leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid parental leave cannot be granted during a deferral period. If both parents are HFSP fellows, each parent is entitled to up to 3 months paid parental leave. Additional childcare time beyond 3 months counts as interrupted fellowship (without HFSPO support). Fellows should inform Fellowship Office and host supervisors/institutions prior to interruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and travel allowance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and travel allowance is intended as a small grant administered preferably as an institutional expense account and is intended for meetings, travel associated with collaborators, computers, research equipment, supplies and other required items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are accountable for use; unspent funds must be returned or are automatically carried over to following year; negative balances can be carried over. Travel expenses should be reimbursed on accrued costs not per diem. Equipment purchased remains property of host institution at end of fellowship unless host permits fellows to keep equipment. Expenses allowed only while fellowship active, with limited exceptions (HFSP meeting during deferral or no-cost extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation allowance eligibility and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocation allowance is a fixed amount to contribute toward moving costs for fellow and family, paid in full with no receipts required; host organization cannot deduct fees and it does not require accounting in financial report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: move to host lab no more than 3 months prior to activation; repatriation or move to another HFSP member country in third year; move after termination—request within six months when submitting final scientific and financial reports (paid after both reports approved). Only granted if fellow does not receive other funds for these expenses; fellow must formally state condition is fulfilled. Specific table of amounts by regions and calculation for spouse/children provided (spouse same allowance; child 2-12 = 50%; child under 2 = 10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and open-access requirement and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of research funded by HFSPO must be published in internationally recognized scientific journals and/or on pre-print servers. An acknowledgement of support by HFSPO must be included in any resulting publication or conference abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees may make articles open-access via open-access journals, posting to repositories, or paying open-access fees to hybrid journals. HFSPO open access policy link provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property (IP) rights policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of intellectual and industrial property rights generated from HFSPO-funded research will be determined by the parties concerned (researchers, institutions) on a case-by-case basis; HFSPO will not assert any claim to IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When collaboration between labs in different countries occurs, ownership or income distribution will be negotiated by collaborating institutions; HFSPO will not become involved in disputes or claim IP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioethical obligations for awardees and hosts
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees and host supervisors must observe the highest ethical standards and conform strictly to codes of practice, regulations and laws governing ethical conduct of scientific research in the host laboratory/institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardee and host are responsible if any regulations are infringed. Joint research should only be undertaken with scientists in countries with experimental procedures acceptable to the host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability disclaimer for damage or injury
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO assumes no responsibility for any damage or injury to awardees in connection with research conducted under the fellowship; awardees release HFSPO of all liability when accepting an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific misconduct definition and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific misconduct means data fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, or any other practice that seriously deviates from commonly accepted research practices. Applicants are expected to adhere to the most stringent international criteria of appropriate scientific conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and policy link provided; applicants should consult HFSPO’s scientific misconduct policy for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of personal data (privacy and research data use)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO is committed to safeguarding personal information in accordance with Directive 95/46/EC; the Privacy Policy explains collection, storage and use of applicant data and awardee data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If research involves collection/processing of sensitive personal data (health, sexual lifestyle, ethnicity, political opinion, religious/philosophical conviction, genetic information, etc.), applicants must justify need, discuss ethical implications, and describe how they will address them in the proposal. For observation involving video/photos, state whether public use will occur and describe privacy/informed consent methods. For existing data, specify sources and whether secondary use authorization exists and is confirmed by primary data owner.
